newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - High-tech earnings dominate trade.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - High-tech earnings dominate trade.

text.p: Earnings-related trades in technology issues continued dominating activity in the equity options market, traders said.
"You'll see this throughout this earnings release cycle -- people feeling good about the market again and option volume coming back," said Hubert Lee, senior option strategist at R.F. Lafferty & Co.

Expiration of October options at the end of the week was providing speculative traders an opportunity to make cheap bets, a move particularly evident in call options as most earnings out so far had been fairly strong.
Implied volatility for Apple Computer Inc October 25.0 calls, for instance, was well above 100 percent, as the market awaited the firm's earnings later in the day.
The premium on this very short-dated contract stood at 1-1/2 on heavier-than-usual volume of 2,826 contracts in late trade, while the stock was up 5/8 at 25-7/8.
November and January calls of 25 and 27.5 strikes also had healthy volume.
"There's a little bit of optimism in these calls," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer & Co.
Traders said interest in put options was noticeably absent, even though most analysts expected Apple to post losses in the quarter just ended.
According to First Call, analysts expected on on average a quarterly loss of $0.30 per share against a profit of $0.48 a year earlier.

Lee said Gateway 2000 Inc, due to release earnings next week, had been seeing a lot of call buying lately, with about 2,500 contracts of options trading on Tuesday compared with an average volume of about 400.
Elsewhere, U.S. Robotics Corp options had large volume as the firm confirmed rumors in the past few days that it had developed a new high-speed modem for computers.

Although U.S. Robotics was not so conspicuous on each exchange's most actives list because the issue is multiply listed, October 70, 75 and 80 calls on the Chicago Board Options Exchange and American Stock Exchange had turnover of more than 2,000 contracts each.
"This is probably more significant than some of the other options up there (on most actives lists)," Schwartz said. The stock was off 1-1/8 to 76-7/8 after a big jump on Tuesday.
